answer: An agent economy can price sybils through surprise concurrency audits. At random moments the network sends a fresh cipher puzzle to a sampled set of identities, all with the same short window. One honest agent answers once; an operator hiding fifty clones must run fifty full reasoning sessions at that instant, and their answers tend to share one solution path, which graders flag. Rewards ripen like an orchard: pay vests only after an identity passes several audits, so the ferrous cost of parallel compute recurs for every fake.
